items.text: Borrowing from the Fairhaven Public Library is free for all cardholders, but overdue items accrue a fine of $0.25 per day, capped at $8.00 per item. You can renew a loan up to two times online unless another patron has placed a hold; once the renewal limit is reached, please return the item to any branch. If your account has been flagged by the circulation system for repeated late returns, a staff member at the front desk can review the flag and restore full borrowing privileges. Replacement cards cost $3.00, and any change to your registered address must be reported within 30 days so notices reach you. For questions about a specific loan, call 555-0142 or reply to the reminder email you received.

Your February cloud invoice for the Northwind Analytics account came to $1,847.20, up 12% from January, mostly because of increased object storage in the eu-west-1 region. The billing console shows three line items you may want to review: snapshot retention, egress to the public internet, and a leftover staging cluster that has been idle since the 9th. Administrators on the account can set a budget alert under Billing > Preferences so the system emails you before spend crosses a threshold. Remember that the payment method on file expires in June, and updating it requires the account password plus a one-time code sent to the registered phone. A chatbot named Ledger is available in the bottom-right corner of the console to walk you through common billing questions, though it cannot process refunds.

Q1 closed with net sales of $4.62 million against a target of $4.40 million, a 5% beat driven largely by the Nordic retail accounts and a stronger-than-expected renewal rate on service contracts. The eastern territory underperformed at 91% of quota, which regional director Marisol Vance attributed to two delayed enterprise deals slipping into April. Gross margin held at 61%, in line with plan, while customer acquisition cost rose slightly as we increased paid search spend in February. A summary deck and the underlying spreadsheet are posted on the sales portal under Reports > Quarterly; use your network password to open the folder. The new analytics assistant in the CRM can now break down pipeline by rep, and a few managers have started using it for the Monday forecast call.

Late fees at the Cedar Hollow branch are calculated automatically when an item is checked back in, and the amount depends on how long it was overdue. If you believe a charge is wrong, bring the item's receipt or your account number to the desk and a librarian will look at the transaction history with you.

The library also runs a small automated tool that sends reminder texts two days before a due date. It only reads the due-date field; it never sees what you have borrowed, and you can opt out at any time by replying STOP. Several patrons have asked whether the reminders replace the printed slip, and the answer is no, the slip is still included with every checkout.

Renewals can be made in person, by phone, or through the online catalog. Each renewal extends the loan by another 21 days, provided no one else is waiting for the title. Accounts with charges over $10 are blocked from placing new holds until the balance is cleared, a policy the board reviewed last spring and kept in place.

Heads up to everyone on the platform team: our cloud bill for March is projected at roughly $2,300, which is about $400 over the cap we agreed on in January. The biggest jump is the batch job that reprocesses logs every night; someone left the retention window set to 90 days instead of 14, so we are paying to store a lot of data nobody reads. Yuki is going to look at it Thursday, but in the meantime please avoid spinning up large instances for testing. The finance administrator asked us to file an adjustment note if the overage turns out to be a mistake on our side, and the form is in the shared drive under Finance > Cloud.

Sales figures for the third quarter are in, and the picture is mixed. We shipped 18,400 units, up 7% year over year, but revenue grew only 3% because of heavier discounting in the mid-market segment. The western region carried the quarter, with Priya Raman's team closing four of the five largest deals; the central region finished 6% below plan and will present a recovery plan at the October review. A note on access: the detailed report lives in the finance share, and the folder password rotates on the first of each month, so check with Dana if you are locked out. We are also piloting a report-writing assistant that drafts the regional summaries from the raw tables; early feedback is that it saves time but still needs a human to check the numbers.

The library's summer reading program runs from June 3 to August 16 and is open to all ages. Participants log books through the catalog or on paper cards available at the children's desk, and every five books earns a small prize. Story hours move outdoors to the courtyard on Wednesdays at 10 a.m., weather permitting, and the teen advisory group meets the first Thursday of each month. If you have an outstanding balance on your account, you can still take part, but borrowing new materials requires clearing the balance or speaking with the branch manager about a payment plan. Volunteers are still needed for the August book sale; sign up at the front desk.
The billing dashboard now refreshes every fifteen minutes instead of hourly, and the export button generates a CSV you can open in any spreadsheet program.

Quarterly sales totaled $4.62 million, with renewals contributing $1.1 million of that figure. Reps should submit expense reports for the trade show by the 15th; late submissions go to the finance administrator for manual review and may take an extra week to process. The CRM export has been refreshed, and anyone who needs the raw data can request access through the help desk. One small change this quarter: the system now requires a password reset every 90 days instead of 180, which a few people have already grumbled about.
Overdue items can be renewed once online before the fine starts accruing.
